subject: Physics
central_question: How do pressure, flow, viscosity and surface effects determine the mechanical behaviour of liquids and gases at rest and in motion?
in_scope_units: 9.1 Introduction — defining fluids and contrasting their compressibility and response to shear with solids.
9.2 Pressure, including Pascal’s law, variation with depth, atmospheric/gauge pressure and hydraulic machines.
9.3 Streamline flow and the equation of continuity.
9.4 Bernoulli’s principle, Torricelli’s law and dynamic lift.
9.5 Viscosity and Stokes’ law, including terminal velocity.
9.6 Surface tension, surface energy, angle of contact, drops/bubbles and capillary rise.
banned_topics: Elastic moduli of solids beyond the brief comparisons used here
Thermodynamic equations of state as a main topic
Detailed turbulence theory beyond the chapter’s qualitative treatment

known_pitfalls.claim: Pressure in a fluid at rest has a fixed vector direction.
known_pitfalls.correction: Pressure is a scalar; the force due to pressure on a surface is normal to that surface.

known_pitfalls.claim: Hydrostatic pressure at a given depth depends on container shape.
known_pitfalls.correction: For a given fluid, pressure difference depends on ρgh, not on container shape or base area.

known_pitfalls.claim: Bernoulli’s equation applies unchanged to turbulent, viscous flow.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter’s Bernoulli relation assumes steady flow of an incompressible fluid with negligible viscosity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Viscosity of liquids and gases changes with temperature in the same way.
known_pitfalls.correction: Liquid viscosity generally decreases with temperature, while gas viscosity increases.

known_pitfalls.claim: Surface tension is an effect of gases as well as liquids.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter treats surface tension as a property associated with liquid interfaces/free surfaces; gases do not have free surfaces of their own.
